name: Back to top
purpose: A page-chrome utility that appears once the reader has scrolled past a threshold and returns them to the top of the scrollable region on activation. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 38, slug back-to-top) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. An Icon-button idiom, per the wave-3 brief: SECONDARY tier tokens (deliberately not primary — this is chrome, never the primary action of a view), 44x44 target and B-D7 press-physics copied verbatim from Icon-button.reference.

props.name: glyph
props.$note: Icon id from the assets/icons sprite. Specimen uses arrows-and-chevrons/arrow-up.svg.

props.name: scrollTarget
props.$note: aria-controls id of the scrollable region this control acts on — the whole page, or a scoped scrollable panel.

props.name: threshold
props.$note: ⛔ UNSPECIFIED store-wide. The scroll distance (px or viewport-heights) past which the control fades in is a UX-writing / Dave call, not resolved here. The demo uses an arbitrary 200px scrollTop for illustration only.

props.name: visible
props.$note: Drives the is-hidden/is-visible fade; true once past `threshold`.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The only tier specimen'd — a solid-but-not-primary control, consistent with 'never the primary action of the view'. Whether a tertiary/quaternary (lower-visibility) back-to-top should also exist is named in decisionsForDave.

tokens.target-size: 44x44 (2.5.8) — the Icon-button floor, unscaled (unlike FAB, which reaches for 56px).

secondary.$note: Copied byte-for-byte from Icon-button.reference's secondary tier.

tokens.elevation: elevation.functional (box-shadow) — a smaller shadow than FAB's, since this control never claims a screen's single decisive action; still needed because it floats above scrolled content.
tokens.radius: border-radius.control — flat/angular (B-D7), same as Icon-button. No corner-deviation question raised here (see Fab.meta for that discussion) — back-to-top is page chrome, not a mobile action-affordance convention.
tokens.placement: 24px bottom/right offset (6 x 4px grid), mirrors FAB — a raw constant, not a token.
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. --target/--glyph and the 24px placement offset are the only non-token values; the appearance threshold (`threshold` prop) has NO value proposed at all, flagged as an open UX question rather than a filled-in default.

motion.hover: scale(1 + press-travel/44) — B-D7 pixel-true, identical geometry to Icon-button (unscaled, unlike FAB).
motion.appear: opacity fade only (no scale/translate) when crossing the scroll threshold — chosen because a moving target near the reader's likely next click is a worse motion hazard than a static fade-in.
motion.reducedMotion: Hover/press transforms disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. The appearance opacity fade is RETAINED (a fade is not itself a motion-sickness trigger the way scale/translate/parallax are) — the click-to-scroll action itself is instant `scrollTo` in the demo, not smooth-scroll-forced (a live implementation should also honour prefers-reduced-motion on the scroll behavior, which the demo's `behavior:'smooth'` does not currently branch on — DECLARED, not fixed).

responsive.rule: Fixed viewport (or scoped-container) placement, bottom-right, 24px offset. Does not reflow — a single always-same-size control regardless of container width.

livesInside: Page (fixed overlay, not a layout child)
mustNotNeighbour: FAB (both are fixed bottom-right floating controls; collision unresolved, see decisionsForDave)

accessibility.name: MANDATORY accessible name via aria-label ('Back to top' default) — icon-only (4.1.2 / 2.4.4).
accessibility.controls: aria-controls names the scrollable region the button acts on (the whole document or a scoped panel) so AT users understand what 'top' refers to when more than one scrollable region exists on the page.
accessibility.keyboard: Reachable in tab order only once visible (a hidden-but-focusable control is a keyboard trap of a different kind — the demo removes it from the flow via opacity + pointer-events:none while hidden, NOT display:none, so it stays discoverable via CSS transition but is inert until shown; whether it should also be visually revealed on :focus regardless of scroll position (so keyboard users are never stuck below a hidden control) is named in decisionsForDave, not resolved).
accessibility.focus: Visible focus outline (text.default), never removed without replacement.

antiPatterns: A disabled/hidden-state glyph bound to a token equal to its own surface (glyph-presence gate, inherited from Icon-button).

display:none while hidden, leaving keyboard-focus users with no way to reach it below the threshold and no way to know it exists above the threshold — the reference uses opacity+pointer-events instead, flagged as the safer default, not proven exhaustively.
Binding the control's scroll target ambiguously when a page has more than one scrollable region (must set aria-controls explicitly).
REVIEW (inferred): shipping WITHOUT ever naming a scroll threshold value, leaving every consuming team to invent its own (the meta deliberately does not propose one either — see decisionsForDave).

tokenValidation.result: PROPOSED — worker lane render-verify only (light+dark, headless Chromium, 0 console errors; the live scroll-threshold demo was driven in the static screenshot only, not interactively scrolled by an automated probe — see receipt UNPROVEN list). _validate_snippets.py / _validate_a11y.py / _validate_type_composites.py / _validate_grid.py / _validate_radius.py NOT RUN by this lane (conductor's serial set, per the wave-3 brief). This is a PROPOSAL, not a proof-of-done.
tokenValidation.$note: Not registered in component-types.json (shared file, outside this lane's fence). Not in _validate_radius.MIGRATED_SNIPPETS. No .cn-back-to-top scope exists in canon.css.

$differsFrom.Icon-button: Same tokens/tier discipline/press-physics MODEL as the secondary tier — but Back-to-top floats fixed above scrolled content (needs elevation.functional), has a SHOW/HIDE lifecycle driven by scroll position (Icon-button is always simply present), and its click action is a scroll command, not an arbitrary page action.
$differsFrom.Fab: Both float fixed bottom-right and share the collision question, but FAB is the PRIMARY tier / the one decisive mobile action; Back-to-top is SECONDARY-tier page chrome that can coexist with (or be superseded by) whatever the primary action of the screen is.

$decisionsForDave: The scroll-distance threshold that triggers appearance is entirely unspecified — a fixed px value, a viewport-height multiple, or something else?
Should the control become focus-reachable/visible whenever it receives programmatic focus, even below the scroll threshold, so keyboard users are never stuck?
FAB vs Back-to-top collision: both are fixed bottom-right. Should Back-to-top always defer (move up/left) when a FAB is present on the same screen?
Should a lower-emphasis (tertiary/quaternary) tier exist for less content-heavy pages, or is SECONDARY the single canonical tier?

usedInContext.$note: Page (fixed overlay, not a layout child)

mustNotNeighbour.$note: FAB (both are fixed bottom-right floating controls; collision unresolved, see decisionsForDave)
